title: Women's Suffrage
objective: After this level you can explain how women won the vote.
summary: New Zealand gave women the vote in 1893 after Kate Sheppard's petition. Britain's suffragists and suffragettes split on tactics; the US and Switzerland followed in 1920 and 1971.

cards.headline: The first country where women won the vote? New Zealand, in 1893.
cards.body: On 19 September 1893, New Zealand women were granted the vote. That made New Zealand the first self-governing country in the world to give women the vote in parliamentary elections. It didn't happen by chance.

cards.headline: 31,872 signatures and a seven-year push
cards.body: Kate Sheppard of the Women's Christian Temperance Union led a seven-year campaign: public meetings, telegrams and letters to politicians, and a steady stream of pamphlets. Its climax came in 1893: 13 petitions with 31,872 signatures in all, the largest ever gathered in Australasia. The main one was reportedly carried to Parliament in a wheelbarrow.

items.label: Suffragists
points: Lobbied Parliament, marched peacefully, petitioned, held meetings

items.label: Suffragettes
points: Led by Emmeline and Christabel Pankhurst
Believed only radical action would force a change in the law
From 1906 to 1914: window-smashing and fires; many went to prison

cards.fact: British women over 30 first voted in a general election in 1918.
cards.context: More than 8 million of them. Men and women still voted under different rules, though. It took until 1928 for every man and woman over 21 to get the vote on equal terms: ten more years.

events.label: New Zealand: women get the vote
US: 19th Amendment bars denying the vote on account of sex
Britain: women and men vote on equal terms
Switzerland: male voters reject women's suffrage
Switzerland: women win the right to vote and stand for election

cards.headline: Women's suffrage: won
learned: Britain: suffragists lobbied, suffragettes took radical action

questions.prompt: The first self-governing country to give women the vote in parliamentary elections was _____.

options.label: the United Kingdom
options.rationale: British women over 30 first voted in 1918.

options.label: Switzerland
options.rationale: Swiss women won the federal vote in 1971.

questions.explanation: New Zealand women were granted the vote on 19 September 1893, a world first for a self-governing country.

questions.prompt: What divided Britain's suffragists from its suffragettes?

options.label: Their methods: peaceful lobbying versus radical action
Their goal: only suffragettes wanted women to vote
options.rationale: Both wanted the vote; their methods differed.

options.label: Their country: suffragists came from New Zealand
Their leader: both groups followed Millicent Fawcett
options.rationale: The suffragettes were led by the Pankhursts.

questions.explanation: Fawcett's suffragists used law-abiding methods; the Pankhursts' suffragettes believed only radical action would force a change in the law.

questions.prompt: Put these wins for women's suffrage in order, from earliest to latest.
items: New Zealand: women get the vote
Switzerland: women win the right to vote
questions.explanation: New Zealand women got the vote in 1893, British women over 30 voted in 1918, the US 19th Amendment came in 1920, and Swiss women won the vote in 1971.
